llm.summary: The skill is an Amazon keyword analytics workflow, but it also has broad external-service, public upload, local persistence, and skill-modification paths that need review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The scripts use environment API keys for remote LinkFox services, allow LINKFOX_TOOL_GATEWAY to control credential-bearing destinations, and pass full inherited environments to helper subprocesses; this is more authority than necessary unless the runtime environment and helper paths are tightly controlled.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: I found no separate install script or hidden install-time behavior; the package consists of markdown skill instructions, Python helper scripts, references, and optional dependencies such as oss2/openpyxl documented in the skill files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main workflow discloses several auxiliary skills, but it encourages automatic keyword expansion, report generation, file upload, vision/PDF handling, and skill creation without consistently requiring confirmation or clear privacy boundaries for sensitive inputs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Several workflows write JSON/XLSX/HTML/session metadata to disk by default, file upload publishes local files to public HTTPS URLs, and the self-extension instruction can modify skill behavior; these are high-impact capabilities despite no evidence of destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core ABA SFR analysis, report generation, ASIN/image entry points, and Amazon suggestion/widget mining are mostly coherent with keyword research, but the package also routes to generic AIGC text/media processing, public file upload, and an expert-skill-creator self-extension step that goes beyond a narrowly scoped analytics skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending Amazon keyword prompts, ASINs, image/media URLs, and possibly local product/report files to LinkFox, Amazon, AIGC, and OSS services. Avoid sensitive or private files unless you explicitly want public URLs, keep LINKFOX_TOOL_GATEWAY pinned to a trusted endpoint, and consider removing or gating the expert-skill-creator self-extension step and automatic upload paths before production use.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded from a pure mismatch: artifact/SKILL.md explicitly names reports, file upload, visual understanding, and keyword-mining helper skills, but those capabilities are broader than the frontmatter summary and need clearer scoping.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for the self-extension pathway: artifact/SKILL.md instructs use of expert-skill-creator to make or revise this expert skill, which is not necessary for ABA keyword analysis and creates capability-growth risk.
[SDI-2] expected: Partly downgraded for bundled suggestion/widget/AIGC helper files because the main workflow references them; not downgraded for generic media download/upload and self-extension authority, which remain overbroad.
[TT3] expected: Remote API calls are expected for LinkFox data access, but the artifact-backed use of environment-controlled LINKFOX_TOOL_GATEWAY with Authorization headers is a real configuration-risk concern rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Image upload, remote image/text analysis, CSV/report export, and public file upload are purpose-adjacent, but the scripts and docs do not consistently add confirmation gates before local files, prompts, media URLs, or keyword strategy data leave the host.
[E2] unexpected: Forwarding os.environ.copy() to helper subprocesses is not required by the business purpose and unnecessarily exposes ambient secrets to child scripts and external dependency paths.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Several trigger rules are broad enough to invoke networked or file-writing helpers on inferred intent, which increases accidental activation risk for public upload, AIGC processing, or report generation.
[SDI-4] expected: The apparent code/documentation mismatch for suggestion and widget miners is largely explained by the main expert skill packaging those tools as declared keyword-expansion dependencies, so this supports review for breadth rather than maliciousness.
